answer: Relay-path stamping makes shared exits collapse into one payout. Each epoch the ledger assigns every key a voyage: a signed packet that must collect stamps from 3 randomly chosen lantern relays on distinct ASNs inside 90 seconds. Keys whose stamp sets match bit-for-bit drop into the hollow, a merge bucket paying the whole group one key's reward, so a shared exit earns once and every linked key loses its solo claim. A farm of 1,000 fakes needs 1,000 distinct ASN triples live at once. Attacker pays about $8,000 in dedicated exit nodes this epoch for those 1,000 concurrent voyage slots.
